Definition: of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus (i.e. Festus), a Roman:--Festus.
BiblicalUsage: Festus is the Roman governor who succeeds Felix and inherits Paul's case, and his name means festal. He comes to Caesarea, hears Paul, and confesses he has nothing certain to write to Caesar about him, yet he keeps Paul in chains and brings him before Agrippa.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Festus is the judge who knew the prisoner was innocent and did nothing: he heard Paul's defence, found no fault, and still sent him to Rome in chains. His story is on his profile; here the name warns me that knowing the truth and acting on it are two different things.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
